excerpts.quote: Windows faces competition from various software products and from alternative platforms and devices.
Our Enterprise Mobility + Security offerings compete with products from a range of competitors
The Windows operating system is designed to deliver a more personal computing experience for users by enabling consistency of experience, applications, and information across their devices.

issues.explanation: These items place Windows and Enterprise Mobility + Security on m365_commercial. The only cited excerpts are competition sentences. They establish that the offerings exist and face competitors, but they say nothing about Microsoft 365 Commercial, so the excerpts do not support the host association. Both items also duplicate item 2, which already covers these components through block 101. The bare 'Windows' attribute is a further problem. It stands for the whole Windows identity, which the source also describes under Windows and Devices. Placing it on m365_commercial narrows a shared identity into one host. The source supports only Windows Commercial (cloud portion and on-premises) under this line.

excerpts.quote: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint competes with endpoint security solution providers.

issues.explanation: Placing Microsoft Defender for Endpoint as a products_services item on m365_commercial asserts that it belongs to that line. The source does not state this association, and the candidate's own unknown unk_defender_segment admits the host is unresolved. The block is in the Productivity and Business Processes competition section, which at most suggests segment context. It does not establish placement in Microsoft 365 Commercial specifically. The item should be an unresolved mention, not an explicit-basis attribute on this host.

excerpts.quote: We compete by providing secure, integrated industry-specific, and easy-to-use productivity and collaboration tools and services
Competitors to Office include software and global application vendors
Microsoft 365 Consumer products and cloud services, including Microsoft 365 Consumer subscriptions, Office licensed on-premises, and other consumer services.

issues.explanation: The statement names 'Office', but the cited excerpt never mentions Office; the Office reference is in an uncited sentence. Office also appears under Microsoft 365 Consumer. Attaching the general 'Office' competition mention only to m365_commercial silently narrows a mention that spans both Commercial and Consumer Office.

excerpts.quote: Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud, comprising Microsoft 365 Commercial, Enterprise Mobility + Security

Microsoft 365 Commercial is an AI-powered business and productivity solutions platform that brings together Office, Windows, Microsoft 365 Copilot, and Enterprise Mobility + Security to help organizations empower their employees.

issues.explanation: Block 093 lists 'Microsoft 365 Commercial' as one component of Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud. That makes it a subset of the node 'Microsoft 365 Commercial products and cloud services', which also includes on-premises Windows Commercial and Office. Block 101 defines the platform 'Microsoft 365 Commercial', and its revenue sentence refers to 'Microsoft 365 Commercial revenue'. The source does not resolve whether that paragraph describes the narrower platform or the whole line, even though it appears under the line's heading. The candidate applies the definition and monetization to the whole node without noting this ambiguity. The description also says '面向企业' (for enterprises), while the source says 'organizations'.

excerpts.quote: Microsoft 365 Commercial revenue is mainly affected by a combination of continued installed base growth and average revenue per user expansion, as well as the continued shift from Office licensed on-premises to Microsoft 365.
Dynamics revenue is driven by the number of users licensed and applications consumed, expansion of average revenue per user, and the continued shift to Dynamics 365
Constraints in the supply chain of device components.
Piracy.

issues.explanation: These monetization items mostly record revenue or growth drivers, not charging mechanisms. Examples include installed-base growth, ARPU expansion, migration shifts, piracy, supply-chain constraints, inventory levels and customer mix. The Skill limits monetization to explicitly stated mechanisms. For Windows OEM, the actual mechanism is OEM purchase of Windows licenses that they pre-install. For Dynamics, it is the number of users licensed and applications consumed. The remaining factors are influences on revenue and should be kept separate from how Microsoft charges.

excerpts.quote: Microsoft 365 Consumer cloud revenue is also affected by the demand for communication and storage through Outlook.com and OneDrive, which is largely driven by subscriptions and advertising.

issues.explanation: The second cited excerpt, 'which is largely driven by subscriptions and advertising', is a fragment with no subject. On its own it cannot support the claim. In the full sentence, the antecedent of 'which' is ambiguous: it could be the demand or Microsoft 365 Consumer cloud revenue. The candidate resolves it as 'demand' without flagging the uncertainty. The first half of the item also records drivers (Office attach rate on new devices, migration to subscriptions) rather than charging mechanisms.

excerpts.quote: Growth depends on our ability to attract new users, understand intent, and match intent with relevant content on advertising offerings.
Our Search and news advertising business is designed to deliver relevant search, native, and display advertising to a global audience.

issues.explanation: The statement includes a growth clause (attracting new users, understanding and matching intent), but the only cited excerpt is the partnerships sentence. The growth clause is therefore unsupported by its cited excerpt. It is also a growth driver, not a charging mechanism. Meanwhile, the business's explicit mechanism, delivering search, native and display advertising, is not recorded as monetization.

excerpts.quote: deliver relevant search, native, and display advertising to a global audience

issues.explanation: The global audience receives the ads; the source does not identify it as the paying customer. Recording '全球受众' (global audience) as customers confuses the audience with customers. The selected text does not explicitly name the paying customer category for this business.

excerpts.quote: The gamer remains at the heart of the Xbox ecosystem.
to benefit our developer and partner ecosystems by providing access to a large customer base

issues.explanation: Block 178 presents the developer and partner ecosystems as partners who benefit from access to Xbox's customer base. They are not customers of Gaming, so listing them under customers confuses partners with customers. The gamer sentence describes users at the center of the ecosystem and does not state that gamers are customers. A 'customer base' is mentioned, but the cited excerpt for c:122 is not a customer disclosure.

excerpts.quote: Our server products are designed to make IT professionals, developers, and their systems more productive and efficient.
Server products revenue is mainly affected by purchases through volume licensing programs, licenses sold to OEMs, and retail packaged products.
a collaboration platform for developers

issues.explanation: Both cited excerpts describe intended users or beneficiaries: server products are designed to make IT professionals and developers productive, and GitHub is a platform for developers. Neither states who the paying customers are. For server products, the source's purchase channels (volume licensing, OEMs, retail) point to purchasers distinct from the end users. Recording these users as customers is uncertain at best and should be qualified as target users or moved to unknowns.

excerpts.quote: strong partnerships with chip manufacturers
Our game content is developed through a collection of first-party studios

issues.explanation: Partnerships with chip manufacturers and first-party studios are not products or services offered to customers. One is a supply-side partnership and the other is an internal content development capability. Listing them in products_services misrepresents what is sold. They belong in context or should be described as capability or partner information.

excerpts.quote: Azure AI offerings provide a competitive advantage as companies seek ways to optimize and scale their business with AI.

We offer supercomputing power for AI at scale to run large workloads, complemented by our rapidly expanding portfolio of AI cloud services (including the latest models) and hardware, which includes custom-built silicon

issues.explanation: The statement labels these offerings 'Azure AI', but the cited excerpt never mentions Azure. The connection to Azure comes from the separate, uncited 'Azure AI offerings' sentence. The cited excerpt alone does not support the Azure label or the placement on the Azure host.

excerpts.quote: In addition to LinkedIn’s free services, LinkedIn offers monetized solutions
Our server products are designed to make IT professionals, developers, and their systems more productive and efficient.
GitHub and Nuance Healthcare include both cloud and on-premises offerings.
along with providing training and certification to developers and IT professionals on various Microsoft products
Our devices are designed to enable people and organizations to connect to the people and content that matter most using Windows and integrated Microsoft products and services.
Gaming, including Xbox hardware and Xbox content and services

issues.explanation:
Each of these descriptions asserts content that its cited excerpt does not contain. The quotes above are the uncited source text that would support each addition:
- LinkedIn: free services plus monetized solutions.
- Server products: the productivity purpose.
- GitHub and Nuance Healthcare: both cloud and on-premises offerings.
- Enterprise and partner services: training and certification.
- Devices: connecting people and organizations via Windows.
- Gaming: Xbox hardware and Xbox content and services.
The claim_evidence must include excerpts that support the entire description.

excerpts.quote: GitHub cloud services, Nuance Healthcare cloud services
GitHub and Nuance Healthcare include both cloud and on-premises offerings.
Nuance professional services

issues.explanation: The source endpoints are the whole github and nuance_healthcare nodes, whose definitions cover both cloud and on-premises offerings. The source only places their cloud services in Server products and cloud services. The edge descriptions and rationale narrow the relationship to the cloud portion. That edge qualifier cannot narrow a whole endpoint, so the relationship asserts that all of GitHub and all of Nuance Healthcare are part of server_cloud. That is unsupported. The on-premises portions might fall under 'other on-premises offerings', but the source does not say so. Nuance also appears in enterprise_partner_services. The fix is to use cloud-subset endpoints or leave whole-identity placement as an unknown.

excerpts.quote: Nuance conversational AI and ambient intelligent solutions
Nuance Healthcare provides AI solutions to the healthcare industry.

issues.explanation: The source refers to 'Nuance conversational AI and ambient intelligent solutions' without tying them to Nuance Healthcare or the healthcare industry. Placing them on nuance_healthcare asserts an identity and association the source does not state. Whether these solutions are the same as Nuance Healthcare's AI solutions remains unknown and should be recorded as unresolved.

excerpts.quote: Many of these manufacturers are also current or potential partners and customers, including our Windows OEMs.

issues.explanation: Block 183 is dispositioned only as competitor context. It nevertheless states an issuer-specific fact: device manufacturers, including Windows OEMs, are current or potential partners and customers as well as Devices competitors. This customer/partner/competitor overlap is not preserved on any node or unknown.
